sentences.zh: 世忠然之，遣元率兵五百，長戟居中，翼以弓矢，自下趨高，賊眾莫支。

translations.literal: Shizhong agreed and sent Yuan with five hundred troops, long halberds in the center flanked by bowmen, advancing from below toward the heights; the bandit masses could not withstand them.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong agreed and sent Yuan with five hundred troops, long halberds in the center flanked by bowmen, advancing from below toward the heights. The bandit masses could not withstand them.

sentences.zh: 乃據望樓，立赤幟，四面並進，賊遂平。

translations.literal: They then seized the watch towers, raised red banners, and advanced on all sides; the bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: They then seized the watch towers, raised red banners, and advanced on all sides. The bandits were pacified.

sentences.zh: 改相州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was changed to observation commissioner of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to observation commissioner of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紹興四年，金人、偽齊合兵入侵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxing the Jurchens and the puppet Qi combined forces to invade.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Shaoxing the Jurchens and the puppet Qi combined forces to invade.

sentences.zh: 世忠自鎮江趨揚州，命元屯承州。

translations.literal: Shizhong hurried from Zhenjiang toward Yangzhou and ordered Yuan to encamp at Cheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong hurried from Zhenjiang toward Yangzhou and ordered Yuan to encamp at Cheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 金人至近郊，元度翌日必至城下，遣百人伏要路，百人伏嶽廟，自以四百人伏路隅。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens reached the suburbs, Yuan estimated they would reach the walls the next day; he sent a hundred men in ambush on the vital road, a hundred in ambush at the Yue Temple, and himself with four hundred in ambush at the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens reached the suburbs, Yuan estimated they would reach the walls the next day. He sent a hundred men in ambush on the vital road, a hundred in ambush at the Yue Temple, and himself with four hundred in ambush at the roadside.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「俟金人過，我當先出掩之。

translations.literal: He ordered: 'Wait until the Jurchens pass; I will first come out and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered, 'Wait until the Jurchens pass. I will first come out and strike them.

sentences.zh: 伏要路者，視我麾旂，則立幟以待，金人必自嶽廟走，伏者背出。」

translations.literal: Those ambushed on the vital road, when they see my banner, should raise flags and wait; the Jurchens will surely flee toward the Yue Temple, and the ambushers should emerge from behind.'
translations.idiomatic: Those ambushed on the vital road, when they see my banner, should raise flags and wait. The Jurchens will surely flee toward the Yue Temple, and the ambushers should emerge from behind.'

sentences.zh: 又決河岸遏其歸路。

translations.literal: He also broke the riverbank to block their return route.
translations.idiomatic: He also broke the riverbank to block their return route.

sentences.zh: 金人果走城下，伏發，金人進退無路，乃走嶽廟，元追之，獲百四十八人，止遣二人。

translations.literal: The Jurchens indeed fled toward the walls; the ambush was sprung. The Jurchens had no way to advance or retreat and fled toward the Yue Temple; Yuan pursued and captured 148 men, sending back only two.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens indeed fled toward the walls and the ambush was sprung. They had no way to advance or retreat and fled toward the Yue Temple. Yuan pursued and captured 148 men, sending back only two.

sentences.zh: 時城中兵不滿三千，金萬戶黑頭虎直造城下約降。

translations.literal: At that time the troops in the city numbered less than three thousand; the Jurchen myriarch Heitou Hu came straight to the walls to negotiate surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the troops in the city numbered less than three thousand. The Jurchen myriarch Heitou Hu came straight to the walls to negotiate surrender.

sentences.zh: 元匿其兵，以微服出，偽若降者。

translations.literal: Yuan hid his troops, went out in plain dress, and pretended to be one who would surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan hid his troops, went out in plain dress, and pretended to be one who would surrender.

sentences.zh: 金人稍懈，俄伏發，擒黑頭虎。

translations.literal: The Jurchens relaxed slightly; soon the ambush was sprung and Heitou Hu was captured.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens relaxed slightly. Soon the ambush was sprung and Heitou Hu was captured.

sentences.zh: 未幾，金兵四集，元戰卻之，追北數十里，金人赴水死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Before long Jurchen troops gathered on four sides; Yuan fought them off, pursued north several tens of li, and many Jurchens drowned entering the water.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jurchen troops gathered on four sides. Yuan fought them off, pursued north several tens of li, and many Jurchens drowned entering the water.

sentences.zh: 改同州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was changed to observation commissioner of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to observation commissioner of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六年，從世忠出下邳，以數百騎破敵伏兵，授保順軍承宣使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Shizhong out from Xiapi and with several hundred horsemen broke the enemy's ambush troops; he was appointed commissioner-in-chief of the Baoshun Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he followed Shizhong out from Xiapi and with several hundred horsemen broke the enemy's ambush troops. He was appointed commissioner-in-chief of the Baoshun Army.

sentences.zh: 十年，略地淮陽，至劉冷莊，騎才三百，當敵騎數千。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he raided Huaiyang and reached Liuleng Village with only three hundred horsemen facing several thousand enemy horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he raided Huaiyang and reached Liuleng Village with only three hundred horsemen facing several thousand enemy horsemen.

sentences.zh: 元揮戈大呼，眾爭奮，敵披靡。

translations.literal: Yuan waved his spear and shouted; the masses vied in ardor and the enemy collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan waved his spear and shouted. The masses vied in ardor and the enemy collapsed.

sentences.zh: 俄而救至，後部疑懼，元回顧曰：「我在此，若等無慮。」

translations.literal: Soon relief arrived; the rear ranks were doubtful and afraid. Yuan looked back and said: 'I am here; you need not worry.'
translations.idiomatic: Soon relief arrived. The rear ranks were doubtful and afraid. Yuan looked back and said, 'I am here; you need not worry.'

sentences.zh: 眾乃安。

translations.literal: The masses then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The masses then settled.

sentences.zh: 轉戰自辰至午，敵退，成列而還。

translations.literal: They fought from the chen hour to the wu hour; the enemy withdrew and they returned in formation.
translations.idiomatic: They fought from the chen hour to the wu hour. The enemy withdrew and they returned in formation.

sentences.zh: 加龍、神衛四廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to overall commander of the four divisions of the Dragon and Divine Guard Armies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to overall commander of the four divisions of the Dragon and Divine Guard Armies.

sentences.zh: 明年，世忠罷兵柄為樞密使，以元為鎮江府駐劄御前諸軍都統制，以統其眾。

translations.literal: The next year Shizhong relinquished military power and became commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Yuan was made overall commander of the imperial armies stationed at Zhenjiang Prefecture to command his followers.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Shizhong relinquished military power and became commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Yuan was made overall commander of the imperial armies stationed at Zhenjiang Prefecture to command his followers.

sentences.zh: 又明年，進侍衛親軍馬步軍都虞候，尋授保信軍節度使。

translations.literal: The year after that he was promoted to chief adjutant of the Imperial Guard horse and foot and soon appointed military governor of the Baoxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he was promoted to chief adjutant of the Imperial Guard horse and foot and soon appointed military governor of the Baoxin Army.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: He died at fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈檢校少保。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made honorary junior guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made honorary junior guardian.

sentences.zh: 曲端字正甫，鎮戎人。

translations.literal: Qu Duan, styled Zhengfu, was a native of Zhenrong.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Duan, styled Zhengfu, came from Zhenrong.

sentences.zh: 父渙，任左班殿直，戰死。

translations.literal: His father Huan served as Left Court Attendant and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huan served as Left Court Attendant and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 端三歲，授三班借職。

translations.literal: At three Duan was appointed provisional third-rank attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At three Duan was appointed provisional third-rank attendant.

sentences.zh: 警敏知書，善屬文，長於兵略，曆秦鳳路隊將、涇原路通安砦兵馬臨押，權涇原路第三將。

translations.literal: Alert and clever, he knew books, was skilled at literary composition, and excelled in military strategy; he served as company commander on the Qinfeng Circuit, temporary inspector of horse at Tong'an Stockade on the Jingyuan Circuit, and acting third commander of the Jingyuan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Alert and clever, he knew books, was skilled at literary composition, and excelled in military strategy. He served as company commander on the Qinfeng Circuit, temporary inspector of horse at Tong'an Stockade on the Jingyuan Circuit, and acting third commander of the Jingyuan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 夏人入寇涇原，帥司調統制李庠捍禦，端在遣中。

translations.literal: When the Tanguts invaded Jingyuan, the commandery dispatched overall controller Li Kuang to defend; Duan was among those sent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tanguts invaded Jingyuan, the commandery dispatched overall controller Li Kuang to defend. Duan was among those sent.

sentences.zh: 庠駐兵柏林堡，斥堠不謹，為夏人所薄，兵大潰，端力戰敗之，整軍還。

translations.literal: Kuang encamped at Bolin Fort; outposts were not careful and the Tanguts pressed him; the army collapsed in great rout. Duan fought fiercely and defeated them, reformed the army, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang encamped at Bolin Fort. Outposts were not careful and the Tanguts pressed him; the army collapsed in great rout. Duan fought fiercely and defeated them, reformed the army, and returned.

sentences.zh: 夏人再入寇，西安州、懷德軍相繼陷沒。

translations.literal: The Tanguts invaded again; Xi'an Prefecture and Huaide Army fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Tanguts invaded again. Xi'an Prefecture and Huaide Army fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 鎮戎當敵要衝，無守將，經略使席貢疾柏林功，奏端知鎮戎軍兼經略司統制官。

translations.literal: Zhenrong stood at the enemy's vital crossing yet had no defending general; Pacification Commissioner Xi Gong, valuing the Bolin achievement, memorialized that Duan should govern Zhenrong Army and concurrently serve as overall controller of the pacification commission.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenrong stood at the enemy's vital crossing yet had no defending general. Pacification Commissioner Xi Gong, valuing the Bolin achievement, memorialized that Duan should govern Zhenrong Army and concurrently serve as overall controller of the pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年十二月，婁宿攻陝西。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Jianyan, Lousu attacked Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first year of Jianyan (1127), Lousu attacked Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，入長安、鳳翔，關、隴大震。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year he entered Chang'an and Fengxiang; Guan and Long were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year he entered Chang'an and Fengxiang, and Guan and Long were thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 二月，義兵起，金人自鞏東還。

translations.literal: In the second month righteous militias rose, and the Jurchens returned east from Gong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month righteous militias rose, and the Jurchens withdrew east from Gong.

sentences.zh: 端時治兵涇原，招流民潰卒，所過人供糧秸，道不拾遺。

translations.literal: Duan was then drilling troops on Jingyuan, recruiting displaced people and routed soldiers; wherever he passed the people supplied grain and fodder, and nothing was left on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Duan was then drilling troops on Jingyuan, recruiting displaced people and routed soldiers. Wherever he passed the people supplied grain and fodder, and nothing was left on the road.

sentences.zh: 金遊騎入境，端遣副將吳玠據清溪嶺與戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Jurchen raiding horsemen entered the border; Duan sent his deputy Wu Jie to hold Qingxi Ridge and give battle, crushing them.
translations.idiomatic: Jurchen raiding horsemen entered the border. Duan sent his deputy Wu Jie to hold Qingxi Ridge and give battle, crushing them.

sentences.zh: 端乘其退，遂下兵秦州，而義兵已復長安、鳳翔。

translations.literal: Duan pressed their retreat and thereupon led troops down into Qin Prefecture, while the righteous militias had already recovered Chang'an and Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Duan pressed their retreat and led troops down into Qin Prefecture, while the righteous militias had already recovered Chang'an and Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 統領官劉希亮自鳳翔歸，端斬之。

translations.literal: Overall commander Liu Xiliang returned from Fengxiang; Duan executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Overall commander Liu Xiliang returned from Fengxiang, and Duan executed him.

sentences.zh: 六月，以集英殿修撰知延安府。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was made drafting academician of the Hall for Assembled Excellence and prefect of Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was made drafting academician of the Hall for Assembled Excellence and appointed prefect of Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 王庶為龍圖閣待制，節制陝西六路軍馬。

translations.literal: Wang Shu was a Hanlin Academy attendant and commanded the horse and foot of the six Shaanxi circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu was a Hanlin Academy attendant and commanded the horse and foot of the six Shaanxi circuits.

sentences.zh: 遂授端吉州團練使，充節制司都統制，端雅不欲屬庶。

translations.literal: Duan was thereupon appointed regimental commissioner of Ji Prefecture and overall commander of the command commission, but Duan had never wished to belong to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Duan was thereupon appointed regimental commissioner of Ji Prefecture and overall commander of the command commission, but Duan had never wished to belong to Shu.

sentences.zh: 九月，金人攻陝西，庶召端會雍、耀間，端辭以未受命。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Jurchens attacked Shaanxi; Shu summoned Duan to meet between Yong and Yao, but Duan declined on grounds that he had not yet received orders.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Jurchens attacked Shaanxi. Shu summoned Duan to meet between Yong and Yao, but Duan declined on grounds that he had not yet received orders.

sentences.zh: 庶以鄜延兵先至龍坊，端又稱已奏乞回避，席貢別遣統制官龐世才將步騎萬人來會。

translations.literal: Shu had Yanyan troops arrive first at Longfang; Duan again said he had memorialized requesting to withdraw and Xi Gong separately dispatched overall controller Pang Shicai with ten thousand infantry and cavalry to join.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had Yanyan troops arrive first at Longfang. Duan again said he had memorialized requesting to withdraw and Xi Gong separately dispatched overall controller Pang Shicai with ten thousand infantry and cavalry to join.

sentences.zh: 庶無如之何，則檄貢勒端還舊任，遣陝西節制司將官賀師範趨耀，別將王宗尹趨白水，且令原、慶出師為援，二帥各遣偏將劉仕忠、寇鯶來與師範會。

translations.literal: Shu could do nothing, then ordered Gong to compel Duan back to his old post, sent Shaanxi command commission general He Shifan toward Yao, and separately sent Wang Zongyin toward Baishui, also ordering Yuan and Qing circuits to send troops as relief; the two commanders each sent deputy generals Liu Shizhong and Kou Zhen to join Shifan.
translations.idiomatic: Shu could do nothing, then ordered Gong to compel Duan back to his old post, sent Shaanxi command commission general He Shifan toward Yao, and separately sent Wang Zongyin toward Baishui, also ordering Yuan and Qing circuits to send troops as relief. The two commanders each sent deputy generals Liu Shizhong and Kou Zhen to join Shifan.

sentences.zh: 庶欲往耀督戰，已行，會龐世才兵至邠，端中悔，以狀白庶，言已赴軍前，庶乃止。

translations.literal: Shu wished to go to Yao to supervise the battle and had already set out when Pang Shicai's troops reached Bin; Duan halfway regretted it and reported to Shu in a memorial that he had already gone to the front, and Shu then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shu wished to go to Yao to supervise the battle and had already set out when Pang Shicai's troops reached Bin. Duan halfway regretted it and reported to Shu in a memorial that he had already gone to the front, and Shu then stopped.

sentences.zh: 師範輕敵不戒，卒遇敵于八公原，戰死，二將各引去，端遂得涇原兵柄。

translations.literal: Shifan treated the enemy lightly and was unguarded; he suddenly met the enemy at Bagong Plain, died in battle, and the two generals each withdrew. Duan thereupon obtained control of the Jingyuan troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan treated the enemy lightly and was unguarded. He suddenly met the enemy at Bagong Plain, died in battle, and the two generals each withdrew. Duan thereupon obtained control of the Jingyuan troops.

sentences.zh: 十一月，金諜知端、庶不協，並兵攻鄜延。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Jurchen spies learned that Duan and Shu were not in harmony and combined forces to attack Yanyan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Jurchen spies learned that Duan and Shu were not in harmony and combined forces to attack Yanyan.

sentences.zh: 時端盡統涇原精兵，駐淳化。

translations.literal: At that time Duan fully commanded the picked troops of Jingyuan and encamped at Chunhua.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Duan fully commanded the picked troops of Jingyuan and encamped at Chunhua.

sentences.zh: 庶日移文趣其進，又遣使臣、進士十數輩往說端，端不聽。

translations.literal: Shu daily sent documents urging his advance and also sent more than ten envoys and jinshi graduates to persuade Duan; Duan would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Shu daily sent documents urging his advance and also sent more than ten envoys and jinshi graduates to persuade Duan. Duan would not listen.

sentences.zh: 庶知事急，又遣屬官魚濤督師，端陽許而實無行意。

translations.literal: Shu knew matters were urgent and again sent subordinate official Yu Tao to supervise the army; Duan outwardly assented but in fact had no intention of marching.
translations.idiomatic: Shu knew matters were urgent and again sent subordinate official Yu Tao to supervise the army. Duan outwardly assented but in fact had no intention of marching.

sentences.zh: 權轉運判官張彬為端隨軍應副，問以師期。

translations.literal: Acting Transport Vice Commissioner Zhang Bin served as Duan's army supply officer and asked about the date of campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Transport Vice Commissioner Zhang Bin served as Duan's army supply officer and asked about the date of campaign.

sentences.zh: 端笑謂彬曰：「公視端所部，孰與李綱救太原兵乎？」

translations.literal: Duan smiled and said to Bin: 'Compare my command with Li Gang's troops relieving Taiyuan—which is greater?'
translations.idiomatic: Duan smiled and said to Bin, 'Compare my command with Li Gang's troops relieving Taiyuan—which is greater?'

sentences.zh: 彬曰：「不及也。」

translations.literal: Bin said: 'It does not reach that.'
translations.idiomatic: Bin said, 'It does not reach that.'

sentences.zh: 端曰：「綱召天下兵，不度而往，以取敗。

translations.literal: Duan said: 'Gang summoned the armies of the realm and went without measuring and thus met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Duan said, 'Gang summoned the armies of the realm and went without measuring and thus met defeat.

sentences.zh: 今端兵不滿萬，不幸而敗，則金騎長驅，無陝西矣。

translations.literal: Now my troops number less than ten thousand; if we unluckily meet defeat, Jurchen horsemen will charge straight through and there will be no Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Now my troops number less than ten thousand. If we unluckily meet defeat, Jurchen horsemen will charge straight through and there will be no Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 端計全陝西與鄜延一路孰輕重，是以未敢即行，不如蕩賊巢穴，攻其必救。」

translations.literal: I weigh whether preserving all of Shaanxi or the Yanyan route is more important; that is why I dare not march at once. Better to destroy the bandits' nest and attack where they must rescue.'
translations.idiomatic: I weigh whether preserving all of Shaanxi or the Yanyan route is more important; that is why I dare not march at once. Better to destroy the bandits' nest and attack where they must rescue.'

sentences.zh: 乃遣吳玠攻華州，拔之。

translations.literal: He then sent Wu Jie to attack Hua Prefecture and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Wu Jie to attack Hua Prefecture and took it.

sentences.zh: 端自分蒲城而不攻，引兵趨耀之同官，復迂路由邠之三水與玠會襄樂。

translations.literal: Duan himself divided forces at Pucheng without attacking, led troops toward Tongguan in Yao, and again by a roundabout route through Sanshui in Bin joined Jie at Xiangle.
translations.idiomatic: Duan himself divided forces at Pucheng without attacking, led troops toward Tongguan in Yao, and again by a roundabout route through Sanshui in Bin joined Jie at Xiangle.

sentences.zh: 金攻延安急，庶收散亡往援。

translations.literal: The Jurchens pressed the attack on Yan'an urgently; Shu gathered scattered survivors and went to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens pressed the attack on Yan'an urgently. Shu gathered scattered survivors and went to the relief.

sentences.zh: 溫州觀察使、知鳳翔府王𤫉將所部發興元，比庶至甘泉，而延安已陷。

translations.literal: Wen Prefecture observation commissioner and Fengxiang prefect Wang Shen led his command out from Xingyuan; by the time Shu reached Ganquan, Yan'an had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Prefecture observation commissioner and Fengxiang prefect Wang Shen led his command out from Xingyuan. By the time Shu reached Ganquan, Yan'an had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 庶無所歸，以軍付𤫉，自將百騎與官屬馳赴襄樂勞軍。

translations.literal: Shu had nowhere to return; he entrusted the army to Shen and personally led a hundred horsemen with his staff in a gallop to Xiangle to encourage the army.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had nowhere to return. He entrusted the army to Shen and personally led a hundred horsemen with his staff in a gallop to Xiangle to encourage the army.

sentences.zh: 庶猶以節制望端，欲倚以自副，端彌不平。

translations.literal: Shu still looked to his command authority toward Duan and wished to rely on him as deputy; Duan was all the more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Shu still looked to his command authority toward Duan and wished to rely on him as deputy. Duan was all the more resentful.

sentences.zh: 端號令素嚴，入壁者，雖貴不敢馳。

translations.literal: Duan's orders had always been strict; those entering the walls, however noble, dared not gallop.
translations.idiomatic: Duan's orders had always been strict. Those entering the walls, however noble, dared not gallop.

sentences.zh: 庶至，端令每門減其從騎之半，及帳下，僅數騎而已。

translations.literal: When Shu arrived, Duan ordered each gate to reduce his escort by half; by the time he reached the tent there were only a few horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu arrived, Duan ordered each gate to reduce his escort by half. By the time he reached the tent there were only a few horsemen.

sentences.zh: 端猶虛中軍以居庶，庶坐帳中，端先以戎服趨於庭，即而與張彬及走馬承受公事高中立同見帳中。

translations.literal: Duan still vacated the middle army tent for Shu to occupy; Shu sat in the tent. Duan first came in military dress hurrying into the courtyard, then with Bin and palace courier Gao Zhongli together entered the tent to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Duan still vacated the middle army tent for Shu to occupy. Shu sat in the tent. Duan first came in military dress hurrying into the courtyard, then with Bin and palace courier Gao Zhongli together entered the tent to see him.

sentences.zh: 良久，端聲色俱厲，問庶延安失守狀，曰：「節制固知愛身，不知愛天子城乎？」

translations.literal: After a long while Duan's voice and countenance both grew stern; he asked Shu about the loss of Yan'an and said: 'The commander surely knows how to love himself but not how to love the Son of Heaven's city?'
translations.idiomatic: After a long while Duan's voice and countenance both grew stern. He asked Shu about the loss of Yan'an and said, 'The commander surely knows how to love himself but not how to love the Son of Heaven's city?'

sentences.zh: 庶曰：「吾數令不從，誰其愛身者？」

translations.literal: Shu said: 'I ordered many times and was not obeyed—who is the one who loves himself?'
translations.idiomatic: Shu said, 'I ordered many times and was not obeyed—who is the one who loves himself?'

sentences.zh: 端怒曰：「在耀州屢陳軍事，不一見聽，何也？」

translations.literal: Duan angrily said: 'At Yaozhou I repeatedly presented military plans and not one was heeded—why?'
translations.idiomatic: Duan angrily said, 'At Yaozhou I repeatedly presented military plans and not one was heeded—why?'

sentences.zh: 因起歸帳。

translations.literal: He then rose and returned to his tent.
translations.idiomatic: He then rose and returned to his tent.

sentences.zh: 庶留端軍，終夕不自安。

translations.literal: Shu remained in Duan's army and was ill at ease all night.
translations.idiomatic: Shu remained in Duan's army and was ill at ease all night.

sentences.zh: 端欲即軍中殺庶，奪其兵。

translations.literal: Duan wished to kill Shu right in the army and seize his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Duan wished to kill Shu right in the army and seize his troops.

sentences.zh: 夜走寧州，見陝西撫諭使謝亮，說之曰：「延安五路襟喉，今已失之，《春秋》大夫出疆得以專之，請誅庶歸報。」

translations.literal: At night he fled to Ning Prefecture, saw Shaanxi Pacification Commissioner Xie Liang, and persuaded him: 'Yan'an is the throat of the five routes and is now lost. A grandee abroad may on his own authority act as the Spring and Autumn Annals allow; I request to execute Shu and return to report.'
translations.idiomatic: At night he fled to Ning Prefecture, saw Shaanxi Pacification Commissioner Xie Liang, and persuaded him, 'Yan'an is the throat of the five routes and is now lost. A grandee abroad may on his own authority act as the Spring and Autumn Annals allow. I request to execute Shu and return to report.'

sentences.zh: 亮曰：「使事有指，今以人臣擅誅於外是跋扈也，公為則自為。」

translations.literal: Liang said: 'The commissioner's business has its aim; for a subject now to execute on his own authority abroad is domineering conduct—you may do it, but do it yourself.'
translations.idiomatic: Liang said, 'The commissioner's business has its aim. For a subject now to execute on his own authority abroad is domineering conduct—you may do it, but do it yourself.'

sentences.zh: 端意阻，復歸軍。

translations.literal: Duan's intent was blocked and he returned to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Duan's intent was blocked and he returned to the army.

sentences.zh: 明日，庶見端，為言已自劾待罪。

translations.literal: The next day Shu saw Duan and said he had already impeached himself and awaited punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Shu saw Duan and said he had already impeached himself and awaited punishment.

sentences.zh: 端拘縻其官屬，奪其節制使印，庶乃得去。

translations.literal: Duan detained his staff, seized his command commissioner's seal, and Shu was then able to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Duan detained his staff, seized his command commissioner's seal, and Shu was then able to leave.

sentences.zh: 王𤫉將兩軍在慶陽，端召之，𤫉不應。

translations.literal: Wang Shen commanded two armies at Qingyang; Duan summoned him and Shen did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen commanded two armies at Qingyang. Duan summoned him and Shen did not respond.

sentences.zh: 會有告𤫉過邠軍士劫掠者，端怒，命統制官張中孚率兵召𤫉，謂中孚曰：「𤫉不聽，則斬以來。」

translations.literal: When someone reported that Shen's troops passing through Bin had plundered, Duan was angry and ordered overall controller Zhang Zhongfu to lead troops to summon Shen, telling Zhongfu: 'If Shen does not obey, cut off his head and bring it.'
translations.idiomatic: When someone reported that Shen's troops passing through Bin had plundered, Duan was angry and ordered overall controller Zhang Zhongfu to lead troops to summon Shen, telling Zhongfu, 'If Shen does not obey, cut off his head and bring it.'

sentences.zh: 中孚至慶陽，𤫉已去，遽遣兵要之，不及而止。

translations.literal: Zhongfu reached Qingyang; Shen had already gone and he hastily sent troops to intercept him but did not reach him and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu reached Qingyang. Shen had already gone and he hastily sent troops to intercept him but did not reach him and stopped.

sentences.zh: 初，叛賊史斌圍興元不克，引兵還關中。

translations.literal: Earlier, the rebel bandit Shi Bin besieged Xingyuan without success and led troops back to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the rebel bandit Shi Bin besieged Xingyuan without success and led troops back to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 義兵統領張宗諤誘斌如長安而散其眾，欲徐圖之。

translations.literal: Righteous-army commander Zhang Zong'e lured Bin to Chang'an and dispersed his masses, wishing to take him gradually.
translations.idiomatic: Righteous-army commander Zhang Zong'e lured Bin to Chang'an and dispersed his masses, wishing to take him gradually.

sentences.zh: 端遣吳玠襲斌擒之，端自襲宗諤殺之。

translations.literal: Duan sent Wu Jie to raid Bin and capture him; Duan himself raided Zong'e and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Duan sent Wu Jie to raid Bin and capture him. Duan himself raided Zong'e and killed him.

sentences.zh: 三年九月，遷康州防禦使、涇原路經略安撫使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year he was transferred to defender of Kang Prefecture and pacification commissioner of the Jingyuan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the third year he was transferred to defender of Kang Prefecture and pacification commissioner of the Jingyuan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時延安新破，端不欲去涇原，乃以知涇州郭浩權鄜延經略司公事。

translations.literal: At that time Yan'an had newly fallen; Duan did not wish to leave Jingyuan and therefore had Jing Prefecture prefect Guo Hao act as commissioner of the Yanyan pacification commission.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yan'an had newly fallen. Duan did not wish to leave Jingyuan and therefore had Jing Prefecture prefect Guo Hao act as commissioner of the Yanyan pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 自謝亮歸，朝廷聞端欲斬王庶，疑有叛意，以禦營司提舉召端，端疑不行。

translations.literal: After Xie Liang returned, the court heard that Duan wished to execute Wang Shu and suspected treason; he was summoned as promoter of the Imperial Camp Commission, but Duan suspected and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: After Xie Liang returned, the court heard that Duan wished to execute Wang Shu and suspected treason. He was summoned as promoter of the Imperial Camp Commission, but Duan suspected trouble and did not go.

sentences.zh: 議者喧言端反，端無以自明。

translations.literal: Counsellors clamored that Duan was rebelling; Duan had no way to clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: Counsellors clamored that Duan was rebelling, and he had no way to clear himself.

sentences.zh: 會張浚宣撫川、陝，入辨，以百口明端不反。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jun pacified Chuan and Shaanxi he entered to explain and with a hundred mouths proved Duan was not rebelling.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun pacified Chuan and Shaanxi he entered to explain and with a hundred mouths proved Duan was not rebelling.

sentences.zh: 浚自收攬英傑，以端在陝西屢與敵角，欲仗其威聲。

translations.literal: Jun himself gathered outstanding men; because Duan in Shaanxi had repeatedly contended with the enemy, he wished to rely on his formidable reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Jun himself gathered outstanding men. Because Duan in Shaanxi had repeatedly contended with the enemy, he wished to rely on his formidable reputation.

sentences.zh: 承制築壇，拜端為威武大將軍、宣州觀察使、宣撫處置使司都統制、知渭州。

translations.literal: By imperial order an altar was built and Duan was appointed Awesome Martial Grand General, observation commissioner of Xuan Prefecture, overall commander of the pacification and disposition commission, and prefect of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order an altar was built and Duan was appointed Awesome Martial Grand General, observation commissioner of Xuan Prefecture, overall commander of the pacification and disposition commission, and prefect of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 端登壇受禮，軍士歡聲如雷。

translations.literal: Duan ascended the altar and received the rites; the soldiers' cheers were like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Duan ascended the altar and received the rites. The soldiers' cheers were like thunder.

sentences.zh: 浚雖欲用端，然未測端意，遣張彬以招填禁軍為名，詣渭州察之。

translations.literal: Though Jun wished to use Duan, he had not yet measured Duan's intent and sent Zhang Bin under the pretext of recruiting and filling the forbidden army to Wei Prefecture to observe him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jun wished to use Duan, he had not yet measured Duan's intent and sent Zhang Bin under the pretext of recruiting and filling the forbidden army to Wei Prefecture to observe him.

sentences.zh: 彬見端問曰：「公常患諸路兵不合，財不足；

translations.literal: Bin saw Duan and asked: 'Your Lordship always grieved that the routes' troops did not combine and funds were insufficient;
translations.idiomatic: Bin saw Duan and asked, 'Your Lordship always grieved that the routes' troops did not combine and funds were insufficient;

sentences.zh: 今兵已合，財已備，婁宿以孤軍深入吾境，我合諸路攻之不難。

translations.literal: now troops are combined and funds prepared; Lou Wusu has led a lone army deep into our territory—we can combine the routes to attack and it will not be hard.
translations.idiomatic: now troops are combined and funds prepared. Lou Wusu has led a lone army deep into our territory—we can combine the routes to attack and it will not be hard.

sentences.zh: 萬一粘罕並兵而來，何以待之？」

translations.literal: If Wanyan Zonghan combines troops and comes, how shall we meet him?'
translations.idiomatic: If Wanyan Zonghan combines troops and comes, how shall we meet him?'

sentences.zh: 端曰：「不然，兵法先較彼己，今敵可勝，止婁宿孤軍一事；

translations.literal: Duan said: 'Not so. In military strategy one first compares enemy and self. Now the enemy can be defeated—this is only the matter of Lou Wusu's lone army;
translations.idiomatic: Duan said, 'Not so. In military strategy one first compares enemy and self. Now the enemy can be defeated—this is only the matter of Lou Wusu's lone army;

sentences.zh: 然將士精銳，不減前日。

translations.literal: yet the officers and soldiers are picked and sharp, no less than before.
translations.idiomatic: yet the officers and soldiers are picked and sharp, no less than before.

sentences.zh: 我不可勝，亦止合五路兵一事；

translations.literal: We cannot be defeated—this too is only the matter of combining the five routes' troops;
translations.idiomatic: We cannot be defeated—this too is only the matter of combining the five routes' troops;

sentences.zh: 然將士無以大異於前。

translations.literal: yet the officers and soldiers are not greatly different from before.
translations.idiomatic: yet the officers and soldiers are not greatly different from before.

sentences.zh: 況金人因糧於我，我常為客，彼常為主。

translations.literal: Moreover the Jurchens depend on us for grain; we are always the guest and they always the host.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Jurchens depend on us for grain. We are always the guest and they always the host.

sentences.zh: 今當反之，按兵據險，時出偏師以擾其耕獲。

translations.literal: Now we should reverse this, hold troops and occupy difficult terrain, and from time to time send partial forces to harass their plowing and harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Now we should reverse this, hold troops and occupy difficult terrain, and from time to time send partial forces to harass their plowing and harvest.

sentences.zh: 彼不得耕，必取糧河東，則我為主，彼為客，不一二年必自困斃，可一舉而滅也。

translations.literal: If they cannot plow they must take grain from east of the river; then we are host and they guest, and in one or two years they will perish of themselves and can be destroyed in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: If they cannot plow they must take grain from east of the river. Then we are host and they guest, and in one or two years they will perish of themselves and can be destroyed in one stroke.

sentences.zh: 萬一輕舉，後憂方大。」

translations.literal: If we act rashly, later troubles will be great.'
translations.idiomatic: If we act rashly, later troubles will be great.'

sentences.zh: 彬以端言復命，浚不主端說。

translations.literal: Bin reported Duan's words on return; Jun did not adopt Duan's view.
translations.idiomatic: Bin reported Duan's words on return. Jun did not adopt Duan's view.

sentences.zh: 四年春，金人攻環慶，端遣吳玠等拒于彭原店，端自將屯宜祿，玠先勝。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year the Jurchens attacked Huan and Qing; Duan sent Wu Jie and others to resist at Pengyuan Station while Duan personally encamped at Yilu. Jie first won.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year the Jurchens attacked Huan and Qing. Duan sent Wu Jie and others to resist at Pengyuan Station while Duan personally encamped at Yilu. Jie first won.

sentences.zh: 既而金軍復振，玠小卻，端退屯涇州，金乘勝焚邠州而去。

translations.literal: Then the Jurchen army rallied; Jie fell back slightly; Duan withdrew to encamp at Jing Prefecture. The Jurchens seized the victory, burned Bin Prefecture, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Jurchen army rallied. Jie fell back slightly; Duan withdrew to encamp at Jing Prefecture. The Jurchens seized the victory, burned Bin Prefecture, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 玠怨端不為援，端謂玠前軍已敗，不得不據險以防衝突，乃劾玠違節制。

translations.literal: Jie resented that Duan did not aid him; Duan said Jie's vanguard had already been defeated and he had no choice but to hold difficult terrain against a charge, and impeached Jie for violating command.
translations.idiomatic: Jie resented that Duan did not aid him. Duan said Jie's vanguard had already been defeated and he had no choice but to hold difficult terrain against a charge, and impeached Jie for violating command.

sentences.zh: 是秋，兀朮窺江、淮，浚議出師以撓其勢。

translations.literal: That autumn Wuzhu spied on the Jiang and Huai; Jun discussed sending troops to disrupt his momentum.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Wuzhu spied on the Jiang and Huai. Jun discussed sending troops to disrupt his momentum.

sentences.zh: 端曰：「平原廣野，賊便於衝突，而我軍未嘗習水戰。

translations.literal: Duan said: 'On open plains and broad fields the bandits are suited to charges, while our army has never practiced river warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Duan said, 'On open plains and broad fields the bandits are suited to charges, while our army has never practiced river warfare.

sentences.zh: 金人新造之勢，難與爭鋒，宜訓兵秣馬保疆而已，俟十年乃可。」

translations.literal: The Jurchens' newly risen momentum is hard to contend with; we should train troops, feed horses, and guard the borders—that is enough; wait ten years before we can act.'
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens' newly risen momentum is hard to contend with. We should train troops, feed horses, and guard the borders—that is enough. Wait ten years before we can act.'

sentences.zh: 端既與浚異，浚積前疑，竟以彭原事罷端兵柄，與祠，再責海州團練副使、萬州安置。

translations.literal: Since Duan differed from Jun, Jun accumulated earlier suspicions and finally on the Pengyuan affair dismissed Duan from military power, granted him a temple post, and again demoted him to vice regimental commissioner of Haizhou, exiled to Wan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Since Duan differed from Jun, Jun accumulated earlier suspicions and finally on the Pengyuan affair dismissed Duan from military power, granted him a temple post, and again demoted him to vice regimental commissioner of Haizhou, exiled to Wan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是年，浚為富平之役，軍敗，誅趙哲，貶劉錫。

translations.literal: That year Jun fought the battle of Fuping and the army was defeated; Zhao Zhe was executed and Liu Xi demoted.
translations.idiomatic: That year Jun fought the battle of Fuping and the army was defeated. Zhao Zhe was executed and Liu Xi demoted.

sentences.zh: 浚欲慰人望，下令以富平之役，涇原軍馬出力最多，既卻退之後，先自聚集，皆緣前帥曲端訓練有方。

translations.literal: Jun wished to appease public expectation and issued an order that in the battle of Fuping the Jingyuan horse and foot had exerted themselves most; after the retreat they were the first to gather—all because former commander Qu Duan had trained them effectively.
translations.idiomatic: Jun wished to appease public expectation and issued an order that in the battle of Fuping the Jingyuan horse and foot had exerted themselves most. After the retreat they were the first to gather—all because former commander Qu Duan had trained them effectively.

sentences.zh: 敘端左武大夫，興州居住。

translations.literal: Duan was restored as Left Martial Grandee and ordered to reside at Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Duan was restored as Left Martial Grandee and ordered to reside at Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年正月，敘正任榮州刺史，提舉江州太平觀，徙閬州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Shaoxing he was restored to regular appointment as prefect of Rongzhou, promoted to director of the Taiping Abbey at Jiang Prefecture, and transferred to Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Shaoxing he was restored to regular appointment as prefect of Rongzhou, promoted to director of the Taiping Abbey at Jiang Prefecture, and transferred to Lang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 於是浚自興州移司閬州，欲復用端。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jun moved his headquarters from Xing Prefecture to Lang Prefecture and wished to reuse Duan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Jun moved his headquarters from Xing Prefecture to Lang Prefecture and wished to reuse Duan.

sentences.zh: 玠與端有憾，言曲端再起，必不利於張公；

translations.literal: Jie had a grievance with Duan and said that if Qu Duan rose again it would surely be unfavorable to Lord Zhang;
translations.idiomatic: Jie had a grievance with Duan and said that if Qu Duan rose again it would surely be unfavorable to Lord Zhang;

sentences.zh: 王庶又從而間之。

translations.literal: Wang Shu also sowed discord from beside.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu also sowed discord from beside.

sentences.zh: 浚入其說，亦畏端難制。

translations.literal: Jun accepted their view and also feared Duan would be hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: Jun accepted their view and also feared Duan would be hard to control.

sentences.zh: 端嘗作詩題柱曰：「不向關中興事業，卻來江上泛漁舟。」

translations.literal: Duan once wrote a poem on a pillar: 'Not building my career in Guanzhong, but coming to the river to float a fishing boat.'
translations.idiomatic: Duan once wrote a poem on a pillar: 'Not building my career in Guanzhong, but coming to the river to float a fishing boat.'

sentences.zh: 庶告浚，謂其指斥乘輿，於是送端恭州獄。

translations.literal: Shu reported to Jun that this pointed at the imperial carriage, and Duan was sent to prison at Gong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shu reported to Jun that this pointed at the imperial carriage, and Duan was sent to prison at Gong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 武臣康隨者嘗忤端，鞭其背，隨恨端入骨。

translations.literal: The martial officer Kang Sui had once offended Duan and was flogged on the back; Sui hated Duan to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: The martial officer Kang Sui had once offended Duan and was flogged on the back. Sui hated Duan to the bone.

sentences.zh: 浚以隨提點夔路刑獄，端聞之曰：「吾其死矣！」

translations.literal: Jun made Sui intendant of penal affairs on the Kuizhou route; when Duan heard he said: 'I am about to die!'
translations.idiomatic: Jun made Sui intendant of penal affairs on the Kuizhou route. When Duan heard he said, 'I am about to die!'

sentences.zh: 呼「天」者數聲；

translations.literal: He cried 'Heaven' several times;
translations.idiomatic: He cried 'Heaven' several times;

sentences.zh: 端有馬名「鐵象」，日馳四百里，至是連呼「鐵象可惜」者又數聲，乃赴逮。

translations.literal: Duan had a horse named 'Iron Elephant' that could gallop four hundred li a day; now he again cried 'What a pity for Iron Elephant' several times, then went to be arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Duan had a horse named Iron Elephant that could gallop four hundred li a day. Now he again cried 'What a pity for Iron Elephant' several times, then went to be arrested.

sentences.zh: 既至，隨令獄吏縶維之，糊其口，熁之以火。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, Sui ordered the prison clerks to bind and restrain him, paste his mouth shut, and burn him with fire.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, Sui ordered the prison clerks to bind and restrain him, paste his mouth shut, and burn him with fire.

sentences.zh: 端乾渴求飲，予之酒，九竅流血而死，年四十一。

translations.literal: Duan was parched with thirst and begged to drink; they gave him wine and he died with blood flowing from the nine orifices at forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Duan was parched with thirst and begged to drink. They gave him wine and he died with blood flowing from the nine orifices at forty-one.

sentences.zh: 陝西士大夫莫不惜之，軍民亦皆悵悵，有叛去者。

translations.literal: The scholar-officials of Shaanxi all lamented him; soldiers and civilians were also despondent, and some rebelled and left.
translations.idiomatic: The scholar-officials of Shaanxi all lamented him. Soldiers and civilians were also despondent, and some rebelled and left.

sentences.zh: 浚尋得罪，追復端宣州觀察使，諡壯湣。

translations.literal: Soon Jun himself met with guilt; Duan was posthumously restored as observation commissioner of Xuan Prefecture with the posthumous title Zhuangmin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jun himself met with guilt. Duan was posthumously restored as observation commissioner of Xuan Prefecture with the posthumous title Zhuangmin.

sentences.zh: 端有將略，使展盡其才，要未可量。

translations.literal: Duan had generalship; had his talent been fully deployed, his measure could not have been known.
translations.idiomatic: Duan had generalship. Had his talent been fully deployed, his measure could not have been known.

sentences.zh: 然剛愎，恃才淩物，此其所以取禍雲。

translations.literal: Yet he was obstinate and willful, relied on talent and looked down on others—this is why he met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was obstinate and willful, relied on talent and looked down on others—this is why he met with disaster.

sentences.zh: 論曰：南渡諸將以張、韓、劉、岳並稱，而俊為之冠。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Among the generals after the southward crossing, Zhang, Han, Liu, and Yue were spoken of together, with Jun as their head.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Among the generals after the southward crossing, Zhang, Han, Liu, and Yue were spoken of together, with Jun as their head.

sentences.zh: 然夷考其行事，則有不然者。

translations.literal: Yet examining their conduct, there are things that do not match.
translations.idiomatic: Yet examining their conduct, there are things that do not match.

sentences.zh: 俊受心膂爪牙之寄，其平苗、劉，雖有勤王之績，然既不能守越，又棄四明，負亦不少。

translations.literal: Jun received the trust of a close confidant and claw; in pacifying Miao and Liu he had merit in rushing to the emperor's aid, yet he could neither hold Yue nor abandoned Siming—his faults were also many.
translations.idiomatic: Jun received the trust of a close confidant and claw. In pacifying Miao and Liu he had merit in rushing to the emperor's aid, yet he could neither hold Yue nor abandoned Siming—his faults were also many.

sentences.zh: 矧其附檜主和，謀殺岳飛，保全富貴，取媚人主，其負戾又如何哉？

translations.literal: Moreover he attached himself to Hui to support peace, plotted to kill Yue Fei, preserved wealth and rank, and flattered the sovereign—how great his perversity!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he attached himself to Hui to support peace, plotted to kill Yue Fei, preserved wealth and rank, and flattered the sovereign—how great his perversity!

sentences.zh: 光世自恃宿將，選沮卻畏，不用上命，師律不嚴，卒致酈瓊之叛。

translations.literal: Guangshi relied on himself as an old general, chose delay and shrank back in fear, did not obey the sovereign's orders, and had no strict military discipline, finally bringing about Li Qiong's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi relied on himself as an old general, chose delay and shrank back in fear, did not obey the sovereign's orders, and had no strict military discipline, finally bringing about Li Qiong's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 迎合檜意，首納軍權，雖得善終牖下，君子不貴也。

translations.literal: He catered to Hui's intent and was first to surrender military power; though he ended well at home, the noble-minded do not esteem this.
translations.idiomatic: He catered to Hui's intent and was first to surrender military power. Though he ended well at home, the noble-minded do not esteem this.

sentences.zh: 二人方之韓、岳益遠矣。

translations.literal: The two men were farther still from Han and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The two men were farther still from Han and Yue.

sentences.zh: 然子蓋、宗顏號俊子弟，著海之功，泗上之捷，亦足稱焉。

translations.literal: Yet Zigai and Zongyan were called Jun's clansmen; the achievement at Haizhou and the victory on the Si are also worth praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zigai and Zongyan were called Jun's clansmen. The achievement at Haizhou and the victory on the Si are also worth praise.

sentences.zh: 王淵以總率扈從有勞，遂至驕盈，失將士心，自取覆敗。

translations.literal: Wang Yuan had merit in overall command and escort, then grew arrogant and lost the generals' hearts, bringing ruin on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuan had merit in overall command and escort, then grew arrogant and lost the generals' hearts, bringing ruin on himself.

sentences.zh: 況結托康履與光世一轍，烏足道哉。

translations.literal: Moreover bonding with Kang Lü followed the same track as Guangshi—how is he worth speaking of?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover bonding with Kang Lü followed the same track as Guangshi—how is he worth speaking of?

sentences.zh: 解元始由韓世忠進，其攻城野戰，未嘗敗衄，有可稱者，不幸早世，惜哉！

translations.literal: Jie Yuan first advanced through Han Shizhong; in storming cities and field battles he never met defeat and has merit worth praise—unlucky to die young; what a pity!
translations.idiomatic: Jie Yuan first advanced through Han Shizhong. In storming cities and field battles he never met defeat and has merit worth praise—unlucky to die young; what a pity!

sentences.zh: 曲端剛愎自用，輕視其上，勞效未著，動違節制，張浚殺之雖冤，蓋亦自取焉爾。

translations.literal: Qu Duan was obstinate and willful, looked down on his superiors, his achievements were not yet manifest, and he repeatedly violated command. Though Zhang Jun's killing of him was unjust, he largely brought it on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Duan was obstinate and willful, looked down on his superiors, his achievements were not yet manifest, and he repeatedly violated command. Though Zhang Jun's killing of him was unjust, he largely brought it on himself.
